config.problem_statement: Given an observational dataset on hospital readmission, can we estimate the average treatment effect of a new discharge protocol, and how robust is the estimate to unobserved confounding?

canonical_transcript.speaker: user:roberto
canonical_transcript.content: Given an observational dataset on hospital readmission, can we estimate the average treatment effect of a new discharge protocol, and how robust is the estimate to unobserved confounding?

content.text: Two structural assumptions are doing load-bearing work: (1) the dataset is observational; (2) any unobserved confounder Z is bounded. I will ask the researcher to confirm (1) directly, and I will also need the critic to surface any co-varying-intervention concerns that would invalidate (2).

direct_requests.content: Is the dataset observational, and do the methods describe any randomization or matching?
What unobserved confounders or co-varying interventions would invalidate the bounded-Z assumption in this hospital cohort?

content.text: The dataset is observational; no randomization. The methods section describes propensity-score matching as a downstream step but the raw assignment is non-randomized. Citing: source_v1.json#methods. Confirming (1).

Confirming observational design (see msg-002). Standard ATE estimators (IPW, AIPW) apply; for unobserved confounding, Rosenbaum bounds and E-values are the canonical sensitivity analyses. I recommend reporting both. No requests outstanding.

I have not yet been asked the logician's question (still queued, I see it in the panel disclosure). My own observation: shift changes, season, and attending physician all co-vary with discharge-protocol uptake in real hospitals. Without naming these, any sensitivity analysis is theatre. I will answer the logician's deferred question in the next round when the runtime drains it.

content.rationale: Round 1 surfaced one resolved fact (observational design) and one outstanding logician-to-critic question still in the deferred queue. The critic flagged co-varying interventions; we need the logician's response after the queue drains.
content.focus: Drain the deferred logician→critic question; resolve the co-varying-intervention concern.

unresolved_disagreements.topic: Sufficiency of propensity matching under unobserved confounding

positions.claim: Matching plus sensitivity analysis is sufficient.
Matching ignores co-varying interventions; sensitivity is theatre without those named.

content.text: Round-open drain: answering the logician's deferred question from msg-001. Three confounder classes that would invalidate bounded-Z: (a) attending-physician practice variation; (b) seasonal admission mix (winter respiratory cases differ from summer cohorts); (c) shift-handover artifacts at protocol-uptake boundaries. Each is an unobserved intervention co-varying with the discharge protocol; (a) and (c) admit fixed-effect adjustment, (b) admits seasonal blocking.

Given the critic's three confounder classes (msg-006), the Rosenbaum Γ-bound framework formalises this exactly: identification holds up to a bound Γ on the odds ratio of unobserved assignment. Attending-physician and shift-handover FE narrow Γ but cannot eliminate it; seasonal blocking helps further. The honest answer is: report point estimate plus Γ-bound, with the Γ-range as the headline. Pretending we identify a point estimate without Γ would be the 'theatre' the critic warned against.

Agreed — IPW point estimate with Γ-bound and an E-value covers the critic's concern. Attending-physician and shift FE plus seasonal blocking are standard additions; I'll specify them in the methods. The honest report is: point estimate plus Γ-range as the headline.

Γ-bounds plus named fixed effects is honest. I withdraw the 'theatre' framing; with explicit Γ this is decision-relevant. Caveat: the report MUST present the Γ-range as the headline, not the point estimate — otherwise readers anchor on the point and ignore the bound.

content.rationale: The panel converged: IPW + Γ-bound + named fixed effects + headline Γ-range. The deferred logician→critic exchange resolved the round-1 unresolved disagreement. The critic explicitly withdrew the 'theatre' framing. Budget is well under cap. Synthesis is appropriate.
content.focus: Synthesize: ATE estimable via IPW with named FE; robustness reported as Γ-range, not point estimate.

resolved_disagreements.resolution: Settled: matching alone is insufficient; matching + named FE (attending-physician, shift) + seasonal blocking + Γ-bound + headline Γ-range is sufficient and honest.

content.integrated_answer: Yes, the average treatment effect of the discharge protocol can be estimated from the observational dataset using inverse-probability weighting (IPW) with the propensity score augmented by attending-physician and shift fixed effects and seasonal blocking. Robustness to unobserved confounding MUST be reported as a Rosenbaum Γ-bound (or equivalently an E-value), and the Γ-range — not the point estimate — should be the headline of the report. Without the Γ-range, readers will anchor on the point estimate and over-interpret the result.
